tasks.short: Meet or correspond with parents about progress and priorities.

steps.what: Click each subject for these children's marks
Read those marks and the children's progress
Choose which progress to discuss with parents
Put the stored guardian address on the invite
Meet parents and guardians and discuss progress
Determine priorities and resource needs with guardians
Correspond with parents about that progress

tasks.design: The {OTHER} pupil record opens one view of this child's stored marks, and the {EMAIL} invite uses the guardian email already on that record. She still reads every mark, chooses what to discuss, and meets or writes in her own words. A missing mark or a missing email means that part stays as it is today.
tasks.previous_blocker: Marks sat under separate subjects and the guardian email sat on another screen, while the talk with parents cannot be handed off.
tasks.enabler_now: The pupil record can show one child's stored marks, and the contact field can fill an invite, without a model writing the judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Parents disagree, a child is upset, and a missing mark or email puts that part back as it is today.
tasks.human_edge: She hears what the guardian is actually worried about and agrees priorities in the room.
tasks.altitude: The week still includes the meetings and the letters. She does less clicking between subjects, and she does not gain a right to skip a conversation.

reach.task: See which resource needs guardians raised this month
reach.learn: Which priorities the class could not meet from its own materials

evidence.claim: Where a pupil record already stores subject, mark and date, one pupil view can replace opening each subject. The teacher still reads the rows.
Systems that evaluate learning outcomes or set an education level are high-risk. This design does not draft the progress talk or set a level.
In the Netherlands, parents and pupils have a say on rules about pupil data. A guardian email is data the school already holds, and other countries have their own rules.

assumptions: The focal work is the teacher's own gathering, the invite, the meeting and the letter. Time the guardian spends talking is not her labour and is not a step.

Mark fields are pupil id, subject, mark and date. The producer is the teacher when she recorded the mark, in the grading task, not in this one. If a subject has no mark she opens that subject as today and the shorter click does not apply.

Invite fields are pupil id, guardian name and guardian email. The producer is the school office at enrolment. That office time is not in this task. If the email is missing she types it and the invite step is not shorter.
Test the pupil record's own pupil view and the mailbox's own contact fill before any custom code. Screen time of those systems is not her labour.
No model writes what she will say about progress. Upkeep is the hour to fix a wrong email or a missing subject.
unknowns: Whether this school's pupil record already has a one-pupil mark view.
What share of guardians already have an email on the record.
research_questions: On a typical parent week, how many subjects does she open per child before the meeting?

already_counted.description: She still opens the one-pupil view and checks the class is right.
She still reads every mark before she chooses what to discuss.
She still checks the guardian name on the invite before it goes.

incremental.description: Fix a guardian email the office stored wrong, and open a subject the view missed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is the meeting and the letter, which stay. The shorter click and the filled email apply only when the mark and the email are already stored. Many guardians still need a typed address, so the high stays at 1 percent.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct and monitor students using equipment and materials.

steps.what: Read the care rules for this equipment
Instruct students in the use and care of equipment and materials
Monitor students so the equipment causes no injury
Stop use that would damage the materials

tasks.design: She reads the care sheet on {DOCS}, then instructs the students and watches them in the room. Nothing is drafted and nothing records how a student handled the equipment. The correction stays with her.
tasks.previous_blocker: The risk is how a student holds the equipment in the moment, and no record shows that in time to stop it.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new removes the need to watch. The care sheet is already a document she can read before the lesson.
tasks.still_hard: A student can still be hurt in the gap between one glance and the next.
tasks.human_edge: She sees a grip or a spill and stops it before someone is hurt or the materials are damaged.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in the week. She still instructs, watches and corrects, and she gains no decision right over safety.

reach.task: Keep the equipment care sheet current
reach.learn: Which rule she had to add in the room because the sheet was out of date

evidence.claim: Watching how a student handles equipment has no standard software path, and a missed correction can cause injury. A model must not invent a safety step.

assumptions: The focal work is her reading, her instruction, her watching and her correction. Student practice time is not her labour.
The care sheet already exists on the document store. The subject lead wrote it earlier. This task does not produce a new rule and does not shorten the telling.
No tool is added, so upkeep is zero. No pupil is recorded while using equipment.
unknowns: Whether the care sheet for this subject's equipment is current.
research_questions: How often does she stop a student for handling that the care sheet does not mention?

already_counted.description: She still reads the care sheet before she instructs the class.

incremental.description: No tool is added, so there is no upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No step is shorter. Instruction, monitoring and the correction stay in the room, and no tool is added, so the net saving is zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet other professionals about students' needs and progress.

steps.what: Copy stored marks and notes into the professionals' brief
Choose which of the students' needs to raise
Mail other professionals the meeting time
Discuss individual students' needs and progress with professionals
Agree the next step for those students' needs
File the agreed action on the pupil record

tasks.design: The {OTHER} pupil record copies this student's stored marks and note sentences into a {DOCS} brief, and she removes any line she will not share. The meeting stays a conversation. If a mark or a note is missing she writes the brief herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: The brief was retyped from the pupil record, and the meeting is a judgement about a child the group knows.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored mark rows and note sentences can be copied into the brief when they exist. The copy adds no need and no label.
tasks.still_hard: A missing note, disagreement in the room, and support details that can be health data.
tasks.human_edge: She decides which need to raise and agrees the next step with people who teach the same child.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays the week. She retypes less when the note is already stored, and she does not gain a right to skip the discussion.

reach.task: Bring the support note the brief quotes
reach.learn: Which note was missing, so the class teacher wrote the brief herself

evidence.claim: A brief can list stored mark rows and note sentences without adding a need. The teacher still decides what to raise in the meeting.
Evaluating learning outcomes is high-risk, and inferring pupils' emotions is banned. The brief copies a stored sentence and does not infer how the pupil feels.
Support notes can be health data. The brief copies a note only when one is already stored, and only for the professionals already in this meeting.

assumptions: The focal work is her brief, her mail, the meeting and the filed action. Other professionals' speaking time is not her labour.

Mark fields are pupil id, subject, mark and date. The producer is the teacher at grading, not this task. Note fields are pupil id, note text and note date. The producer is whoever wrote the support note, often the special education teacher, in an earlier task.
If there is no mark row or no note, she writes the brief herself and this step is not shorter. The copy must not add a need, a level or a diagnostic label.
Test the pupil record's own print of marks and notes before custom code. She still chooses what to raise, and the meeting is unchanged.
Filing the agreed action stays her own typing. Upkeep is rewriting a brief that copied the wrong pupil's note.
unknowns: What share of pupils discussed in these meetings already have a stored support note.
Whether support notes in this school are treated as health data.
research_questions: How often is the brief missing a note, so she writes it by hand before the meeting?

already_counted.description: She still reads every copied line and removes any she will not share.

incremental.description: Rewrite the brief when a copied note is for the wrong pupil or the note is missing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only the retype into the brief is shorter, and only when a mark and a note are already stored. Many pupils have no note, so she writes the brief herself. The meeting, the choice of what to raise and the filed action stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare reports on students and activities for administration.

steps.what: Confirm which report the administration required
Ask what activities a colleague saw
Open each pupil to collect marks for the reports
Read the mark rows these reports must include
Copy mark rows into the report and type activities
Draft the report comment from notes on students

loop.input: pupil id, mark rows with subject, mark and date, activity lines she typed, and her stored note text
loop.check: every sentence is a verbatim span of her note or states a subject and mark present in the rows, and no sentence names a level, a diagnosis or an activity she did not type
loop.stop: two redrafts, then she writes that pupil's comment herself; a missing note means no draft for that pupil
loop.why_not_simpler: a mark table does not write the sentences administration requires, and a fixed template cannot tell which of her notes belongs in the sentence

steps.what: Judge whether each comment on students is fair
Store the signed reports
Mail the administration that the reports are stored

tasks.design: A class-period list on the {OTHER} pupil record fills mark rows on the {SPREADSHEET}, and a bounded draft on {DOCS} may only restate her note or a mark in those rows. She signs that exact text, and only then does {OTHER} store it. The draft does not set a mark or a level, and a sentence that does not trace is one she writes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comments were free text about a pupil, and mark rows were retyped because the report was a separate sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: Stored marks can fill the table, and a bounded draft can only restate a note or a mark she then signs.
tasks.still_hard: Thin notes, activities nobody logged, and a comment that still needs her judgement of what is fair.
tasks.human_edge: She decides whether a sentence about a pupil is fair, and she writes it when the note does not support it.

ambition.what: Sign or rewrite every pupil's report comment in the week administration names the class and period.

tasks.altitude: She spends less of the report week retyping marks and more of it on whether each comment is fair. She does not gain a right to file a comment she has not signed.

reach.task: Name the class, period and report type before she starts
reach.learn: Which reports still needed a comment she wrote herself because the note was missing

evidence.claim: ParnasSys keeps pupil records, an individual support plan module and learning-goal tracking, and no AI is named for it.
A report comment can be limited to a verbatim note or a mark already in the rows. The teacher signs, or writes the comment when the check fails.
Texas machine scoring of state tests was followed by rescoring requests rising from 2,758 in 2024 to 64,489 in 2026, and computers first scored 58 percent of more than 13,300 raised reading scores.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk from 2 December 2027, and a school that adapts an AI tool can become its provider.
Under the Dutch school participation law, parents and pupils have a say on pupil-data rules and staff have a say on tools that can monitor them. Other countries have their own rules.
Pupil report data is processed for the school's public task, support details can be health data, and a new pupil-data tool needs a data protection assessment.

assumptions: The focal work is her confirmation, the colleague conversation, the mark collection, the table, the comment, the signature, the store and the mail. Administration and colleague speaking time beyond her questions is not her labour.

Report-request fields are class id, period and report type. She records them in the confirmation step, and that time stays. Mark fields are pupil id, subject, mark and date. The producer is the teacher at grading, not this task. If the class-period list cannot filter on class and period she opens each pupil and the click step is not shorter.
Activity lines are produced in the spreadsheet step from the colleague's account. That typing stays. The copy step only skips retyping rows that already have pupil, subject, mark and date.

Note fields are pupil id and note text, produced when she wrote the class note earlier. No note means no draft for that pupil. The store step writes only the comment version she signed in the previous step. A later edit voids that store. The store does not fetch new marks.
Test the pupil record's own class-period list before custom code. Its runtime is not her labour. The draft does not set a mark, a level or a diagnosis, and it does not watch a test.
Upkeep is rewriting comments that do not trace and relinking a note to the right pupil.
unknowns: Whether the pupil record already lists a class and period without a custom query.
What share of pupils already have a teacher note long enough to quote.
Whether this school treats the comment as an evaluation of learning outcomes under the high-risk rules from 2 December 2027.
research_questions: For a typical class report, how many pupils have no stored note, so she writes the comment herself?

already_counted.description: She still opens the class-period list and reads the mark rows for the right class.
She still types activity lines the mark list does not hold and checks the copied rows.
She still reads every comment sentence and signs or rewrites it.

incremental.description: Rewrite comments that do not trace to a note or a mark, and relink a note to the right pupil.

approvals.approved_version: signed comment text for this class and period, bound to the mark rows and activity lines she checked

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The comment saving applies only where she already wrote a note. Activity lines stay typed. She rewrites any sentence that does not trace to a note or a mark, and she still reads the rows. Many classes have thin notes, so the high stays at 14 percent, well under the central net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still in the classroom and in parent and staff meetings. A list does not choose what she says, and a report comment is stored only after she signs it.
skills_to_grow: Check that a report sentence quotes her note or a stored mark and adds no level.
Check that a parent invite uses the stored guardian email and does not guess one.
role.ambitious_version: Each administration report starts from marks already stored and a comment she has signed, and each parent meeting starts from the priorities agreed in the room.

job.title: Middle School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
